podcast.title: First Proper Public Performance (March 1968)
podcast.body: The band's first official public performance took place in March 1968. The opening act for this show was unusual: a food processor (blender with water) roaring through the PA system for about 15 minutes. "The first proper public performance came in March of 1968. The opening act for this show was a food processor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extreme Contrast to Mainstream and Hippie Bands
podcast.body: The Stooges, particularly through Iggy Pop's antics, presented a "crazy" and extreme alternative that starkly contrasted with mainstream acts like The Beatles and The Rolling Stones, and was also distinct from the prevailing hippie groups. "This wasn't anything mainstream bands like the beetles or the stones we're doing. And the hippie groups, certainly weren't into this kind of thing either."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Show (Halloween, Year Not Specified)
podcast.body: Iggy Pop formed The Psychedelic Stooges in the summer of 1967, and their first show was a private party held on Halloween. The performance was reportedly so poor that their manager quit and returned to his job as a school teacher. "they played their first show at a private party that Halloween. It wasn't very good, so bad that their manager quit and went back to his job as a school teacher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Iggy Pop's Unusual Stage Attire
podcast.body: During their first public performance, Iggy Pop appeared on stage wearing a nightshirt, golf shoes, white mime makeup, and a large afro wig made from tinfoil. "Iggy was wearing a night shirt and golf shoes and white mime makeup and a big afro wig made out of tinfoil."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Scott Asheton's Drumming Style
podcast.body: Drummer Scott Asheton kept time by banging on a couple of 50-gallon oil drums with hammers instead of traditional drumsticks. "Drummer Scott Ashden kept time by banging on a couple of 50 gallon oil drums with hammers instead of drumsticks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Debut Performance (October 31, 1967)
xref.body: The band, initially called Iggy and the Psychedelic Stooges, made their debut on October 31, 1967, in Ann Arbor, Michigan. They were characterized by a loud, spontaneous, sloppy, fuzzy, arrogant, violent, angry, and powerful sound. "And on October 31, 1967, Iggy and the psychedelic studios made their debut in Ann Arbor, Michigan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Iggy Pop

xref.title: Dissolution and Formation of The Psychedelic Stooges (Summer 1967)
xref.body: The Iguanas disbanded in the summer of 1967, paving the way for Iggy Pop to form his new group, The Psychedelic Stooges. "by that summer, the iguanas were gone and Iggy was in a new band called The Psychedelic Stooges."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Name Origin ("Psychedelic Stooges")
xref.body: The name originated during a drug-fueled session at the Ashton house in 1967 where the band members were watching "The Three Stooges" on TV while high on acid. Initially, they suggested "The Psychedelic Stooges" but it was later shortened to just "The Stooges" as no one could remember how to spell "psychedelic." "When they were very, very high, they were watching the three stuages on TV and somebody suggested I know we'll just call ourselves the psychedelic stuages."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

xref.title: Name Change to The Stooges
xref.body: Shortly after their debut as Iggy and the Psychedelic Stooges, the band's name was shortened to simply "The Stooges," marking the beginning of the legend of Iggy Pop. "The psychedelic studios soon became just the stooages. And here begins the legend of Iggy Pop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
